This pull request introduces several improvements and refactorings focused on supporting an explicit `execution_id` for task and function invocation tracking, as well as codebase cleanups and minor test updates. The main changes revolve around propagating the `execution_id` through protobuf definitions, event handling, function invocation, and execution management, ensuring more robust tracking and correlation across distributed components.

### Execution ID Propagation and Task Event Handling

* Added an optional `execution_id` field to the `TaskEvent` and `InvokeFunctionRequest` protobuf messages to enable explicit tracking of executions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f2d4140fb101a0fa05f2a0492ddd92b19e7246c7509c65a711669ac2b0a76beR107) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-654d48bb22dfb867b22e07c06d357126a3256a5daaebe5fae2d2af6c62ab4e50R101)
* Updated the `StoredEvent` struct and related event bus logic in `src/sms/events.rs` to store and propagate the `execution_id` for task events, generating it for "Create" events. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-70ae34754be72e14fea3912c52751469267fb9cf4353bcdd12f9878483777e45R20-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-70ae34754be72e14fea3912c52751469267fb9cf4353bcdd12f9878483777e45R84) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-70ae34754be72e14fea3912c52751469267fb9cf4353bcdd12f9878483777e45R123-R136) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-70ae34754be72e14fea3912c52751469267fb9cf4353bcdd12f9878483777e45R146)
* Modified the `TaskEventSubscriber` in `src/spearlet/task_events.rs` to extract and use the `execution_id` when handling and executing tasks, passing it into function invocation requests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b67c0e59ace20b41d7994083cc7701809c5e16c480e4732c24921ad30b53d104R139-R143) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b67c0e59ace20b41d7994083cc7701809c5e16c480e4732c24921ad30b53d104L149-R165) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b67c0e59ace20b41d7994083cc7701809c5e16c480e4732c24921ad30b53d104L196-R212) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b67c0e59ace20b41d7994083cc7701809c5e16c480e4732c24921ad30b53d104L217-R230) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-b67c0e59ace20b41d7994083cc7701809c5e16c480e4732c24921ad30b53d104L227-R245)

### Function Invocation and Execution Management

* Refactored `FunctionServiceImpl` in `src/spearlet/function_service.rs` to consistently propagate and utilize the `execution_id` for both sync and async executions, defaulting to a generated value if not provided. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3e6294ef08135f0ebfdab566d247b587b378d5392d80d7ff99bd8dc7bc4c3065L147-L148) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3e6294ef08135f0ebfdab566d247b587b378d5392d80d7ff99bd8dc7bc4c3065L205-R205) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3e6294ef08135f0ebfdab566d247b587b378d5392d80d7ff99bd8dc7bc4c3065L377-R391) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3e6294ef08135f0ebfdab566d247b587b378d5392d80d7ff99bd8dc7bc4c3065L417-R415)
* Renamed the `request_id` field to `execution_id` in the `ExecutionResponse` struct to match the new semantics and ensure consistent usage throughout the codebase.
* Updated the `HttpAdapter` to use `execution_id` for response headers and error reporting, replacing the previous `request_id` usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4799fe60eae8a2eed83d632dd9610b704177cbd577873d74c950213b8d64c1ceL287-R287) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4799fe60eae8a2eed83d632dd9610b704177cbd577873d74c950213b8d64c1ceL301-R301)

author: copilot
body:
Transforms Express-only architecture to support any serverless platform through an extensible adapter pattern while maintaining backward compatibility.

## Architecture

Introduces **platform-agnostic** adapter pattern to abstract HTTP handling across platforms:

```javascript
// Extensible base class for any platform
class BaseAdapter {
  async normalizeRequest(platformRequest) { /* ... */ }
  createResponse() { /* ... */ }
  async handleRequest(platformRequest) { /* ... */ }
}
```

**Built-in Adapters:**
- `LambdaAdapter` - API Gateway v1/v2 event handling
- `WorkersAdapter` - Fetch API request/response
- `ExpressAdapter` - Existing Express behavior (unchanged)

**Extensible to Any Platform:**
- Azure Functions
- Google Cloud Functions
- Vercel Serverless Functions
- Netlify Functions
- Alibaba Cloud Function Compute
- Tencent Cloud SCF
- Any custom serverless platform

## Configuration

```javascript
// vite.config.js
serverActions({
  serverless: {
    enabled: true,
    targets: ["express", "lambda", "workers"]
  }
})
```

## Build Output

Single build generates platform-specific handlers:

```
dist/
├── server.js      # Express (default)
├── lambda.js      # Lambda handler  
├── workers.js     # Workers handler
├── actions.js     # Shared server functions
└── adapters/      # Platform adapters
```

All handlers import same `actions.js`, ensuring identical behavior across platforms.

## Implementation

**Core changes:**
- `src/adapters/` - Platform adapter implementations with extensible BaseAdapter
- `src/serverless-build.js` - Handler generation utilities
- `src/index.js` - Build pipeline integration

**Exports:**
```javascript
export { BaseAdapter, LambdaAdapter, WorkersAdapter, createLambdaHandler, createWorkersHandler }
```

Server functions require no modifications. Client code unchanged.

## Custom Adapters

Create adapters for any platform by extending `BaseAdapter`:

```javascript
import { BaseAdapter } from "vite-plugin-server-actions";

export class MyPlatformAdapter extends BaseAdapter {
  async normalizeRequest(platformRequest) { /* ... */ }
  createResponse() { /* ... */ }
  async handleRequest(platformRequest) { /* ... */ }
}
```

See `docs/custom-adapters.md` for comprehensive guide with examples for Azure, Google Cloud, Vercel, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud, and more.

## Deployment

```bash
# Lambda
sam deploy --guided

# Workers  
npx wrangler deploy

# Express (unchanged)
node dist/server.js

# Custom platforms - use your adapter
```

## Documentation

- `docs/serverless-deployment.md` - Deployment guide for built-in platforms
- `docs/custom-adapters.md` - Complete guide for creating custom adapters
- `docs/examples/aws-lambda/` - AWS Lambda configuration examples
- `docs/examples/cloudflare-workers/` - Cloudflare Workers configuration examples

Configuration examples provided in `docs/examples/`.

## Testing

- 7 new tests for adapter configuration and handler generation
- All existing tests pass (255 total)
- Validated handler code generation for all platforms

body:
## Summary
- Fix double `/api` path bug that caused API calls to return HTML instead of JSON
- Fix staging URL normalization to keep `*.staging.volterra.us` URLs as-is

## Problem
API calls were returning HTML (F5 XC web console login page) instead of JSON responses due to two issues:

1. **Double /api path**: BaseURL includes `/api`, tool paths from OpenAPI specs also start with `/api`, resulting in `/api/api/...` URLs
2. **Staging URL conversion**: Staging URLs were incorrectly converted to `*.staging.console.ves.volterra.io` which doesn't exist

## Solution
1. Added `normalizeToolPath()` helper in `execute.ts` to strip `/api` prefix from tool paths
2. Updated `normalizeApiUrl()` in `credential-manager.ts` to keep staging URLs as-is

## Test plan
- [x] All 1216 tests pass
- [x] Verified with production tenant (f5-amer-ent) - Status 200 ✅
- [x] Verified with staging tenant (nferreira) - Status 200 ✅
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript)

body:
Removes remote server management feature, adds proper restart command, and fixes resource reporting to include child process stats.

## Changes

### Server command removed
- Deleted `src/cli/server.rs` and all server-related command handling
- Simplified CLI by removing remote management capability
- Updated documentation

### Restart command now standalone
Previously an alias of `start`, now a dedicated command that only restarts existing processes:
```bash
opm restart <id/name>  # Restarts process without creating if missing
```

### CPU/RAM stats now include child processes
Added `get_process_cpu_usage_with_children()` and `get_process_memory_with_children()` that recursively aggregate stats across process trees:

```rust
// Before: only parent process
memory_usage = process.memory_info().ok().map(MemoryInfo::from);
cpu_percent = Some(get_process_cpu_usage_percentage(item.pid));

// After: parent + all descendants  
memory_usage = get_process_memory_with_children(item.pid);
cpu_percent = Some(get_process_cpu_usage_with_children(item.pid));
```

Updated stats collection in:
- CLI info/list commands (`src/cli/internal.rs`)
- Daemon health reporting (`src/daemon/mod.rs`)
- API endpoints (`src/daemon/api/routes.rs`)
- Process status structures (`src/process/mod.rs`)

Process spawning 3 child processes now correctly reports ~8.9MB (parent + children) instead of ~1.8MB (parent only).

body:
Adds Discord.js select menu (dropdown) components to replace command-only input for settings and audio filters.

## Implementation

**Type System** (`types/select-menus.ts`)
- Handler interfaces with typed contexts and results
- Union types for all select menu interaction types
- Audio filter and repeat mode enums

**Builder Utilities** (`components/builders/selectMenuBuilder.ts`)
- Menu creation with min/max value constraints and emoji support
- Custom ID encoding/parsing with embedded metadata
- Configuration validation (Discord 25-option limit, min ≤ max, etc.)

**Components**
- **Filter menu**: Multi-select up to 3 filters (bass boost, nightcore, vaporwave, 8D audio)
- **Repeat mode menu**: Single-select (off/track/queue)
- Default value marking for current selections

**Handler System**
- Centralized registry pattern matching existing button handlers
- Metadata extraction from custom IDs: `prefix_key1:val1_key2:val2`
- Integrated with statistics tracking

**Commands**
- `/filter` - Audio filter selection
- `/settings` - Server settings with repeat mode

## Usage

```typescript
import { createFilterMenu } from './components/select-menus/string/filterMenu';

// Create menu with current filters marked as default
const menu = createFilterMenu(guildId, ['bassboost', 'nightcore']);

await interaction.reply({
  content: 'Select up to 3 audio filters:',
  components: [menu],
  flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral,
});
```

Handler registration:
```typescript
registerSelectMenuHandler('audio_filter', async (interaction, context) => {
  const { filters } = validateFilterSelection(interaction.values);
  // Apply filters...
  return { success: true, data: { filters } };
});
```

## Foundation

Builder utilities support all Discord select menu types (string, user, role, channel, mentionable). String select menus implemented; others available when needed.

## Test Coverage

- 63 tests covering builders, handlers, validation, and components
- Handler registration lifecycle
- Edge cases (invalid filters, min/max violations, option limits)

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>Implement select menus for settings and user interaction</issue_title>
<issue_description>## Objective
Add Discord.js select menu components (dropdowns) for better user interaction with settings, filtering, and selection-based commands.

## Current State
No select menus currently implemented. All input is via slash command options.

## Select Menu Types

### 1. String Select Menus
**Use Cases:**
- Audio quality selection (low, medium, high)
- Filter presets (bass boost, nightcore, vaporwave)
- Repeat mode (off, track, queue)
- Saved playlists selection
- Language/region preferences

### 2. User Select Menus
**Use Cases:**
- Assign DJ role to users
- Share queue with specific users
- User-specific permissions
- Collaborative playlist creation

### 3. Role Select Menus
**Use Cases:**
- Configure DJ roles
- Set allowed roles for commands
- Role-based music permissions

### 4. Channel Select Menus
**Use Cases:**
- Set default music channel
- Configure announcement channels
- Log channel selection
- Multi-room music setup

### 5. Mentionable Select Menus
**Use Cases:**
- Flexible permission assignment
- Notification settings
- Whitelist/blacklist configuration

## Implementation Details

### File Structure
```
components/
├── select-menus/
│   ├── string/
│   │   ├── settingsMenu.ts
│   │   ├── filterMenu.ts
│   │   ├── playlistMenu.ts
│   │   └── repeatModeMenu.ts
│   ├── user/
│   │   └── djAssignMenu.ts
│   ├── role/
│   │   └── rolePermissionMenu.ts
│   ├── channel/
│   │   └── channelConfigMenu.ts
│   └── builders/
│       └── selectMenuBuilder.ts

handlers/
└── selectMenuHandler.ts
```

### New Commands to Create

#### `/settings` Command
- Display server settings with select menus
- Options:
  - Default volume (1-100)
  - Repeat mode (off/track/queue)
  - Auto-leave timeout
  - Audio quality
  - DJ-only mode toggle

#### `/filter` Command
- Audio filter selection menu
- Options: None, Bass Boost, Nightcore, Vaporwave, 8D Audio
- Preview option before applying
- Multiple filters support

#### `/playlist` Command
- Manage saved playlists
- Select playlist to load
- Create/delete/edit playlists
- Share playlist with users

### Technical Requirements

#### Select Menu Features
- Min/max selection values configuration
- Placeholder text for better UX
- Default selected options
- Disabled options when not applicable
- Dynamic option generation
- Emoji support in options

#### Handler System
- Parse custom IDs with metadata
- Validate user permissions
- Update message after selection
- Store selections in database/cache
- Handle multi-select properly

### Example Implementation

```typescript
import { StringSelectMenuBuilder, ActionRowBuilder } from 'discord.js';

export function createFilterMenu(): ActionRowBuilder {
  const selectMenu = new StringSelectMenuBuilder()
    .setCustomId('audio_filter_select')
    .setPlaceholder('Choose audio filters')
    .setMinValues(0)
    .setMaxValues(3)
    .addOptions(
      {
        label: 'None',
        description: 'No audio filter',
        value: 'none',
        emoji: '❌',
      },
      {

author: yongkangc
body:
**Problem**
In `MultiProofTask`, `Arc::new(self.multi_added_removed_keys.clone())` is called on every dispatch via `dispatch_with_chunking`. When chunking is enabled (default) and multiple chunks are dispatched, this performs redundant deep clones even when the underlying data hasn't changed.

**Solution**
Cache the `Arc<MultiAddedRemovedKeys>` and only regenerate it when the underlying data is modified (via `touch_accounts()` or `update_with_state()`). Subsequent dispatches within the same batch use cheap `Arc::clone()` instead of `clone + Arc::new`.

**Expected Impact**
Microbenchmark shows ~4.7x improvement when multiple dispatches occur between data modifications:
- 10 dispatches with 2 updates: 14.5µs (dirty-flag) vs 68.9µs (always clone)
- Per-clone cost: ~7µs for 5K keys → ~2.5ns for Arc::clone

author: thewilloftheshadow
body:
Discord has the concept of User Apps, where instead of installing a bot to a server, you can install it to your user account
you dont get the full bot scope, so no reading messages, but you CAN use interactions, aka slash commands, where the user can then run the installed bot's slash commands anywhere in any server. 

I talked with Clawd in the Discord server, and he said that doing a stable slash-session for this was the best idea, so I did this PR.

This PR adds support for Discord User App interactions (slash commands) so users can install Clawdis to their account and invoke it anywhere without bot read access. The gateway listens for chat input interactions via discord.js and replies ephemerally, giving “ask in place” behavior without channel snooping. Each user gets a stable slash‑session key (discord:slash:<userId>), so it behaves like another surface with shared memory but an isolated thread.

Convo start with Clawd: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1456350065223270435/1456526329829658655

body:
### Motivation
- Avoid producing double slashes when resolving the upload endpoint if `API_BASE` or `BASE_URL` ends with a trailing slash.
- Prevent runtime crashes when extracting hosts from image URLs by correctly resolving relative URLs against the page base.
- Keep `fetch` call options clean by not passing unnecessary/undefined `headers` fields.
- Ensure the widget sends only public/non-`data:` image URLs to the Valki API and simplify attachment payloads.

### Description
- Added `resolveUploadUrl()` which trims trailing slashes from `API_BASE`/`BASE_URL` and returns a safe `/api/upload` fallback when neither is defined. 
- Replaced direct `fetch("/api/upload")` and the removed `API_UPLOAD` constant with `uploadFile()` calling `resolveUploadUrl()` and using an `opts` object instead of passing `headers: undefined`.
- Simplified attachment handling by removing `dataUrl`/`previewUrl` from attachments and updating `normalizeImagePayload()` to reject `data:` URLs, plus updated UI preview and send logic to use `a.url` only.
- Improved send-time diagnostics by resolving hosts with `new URL(img.url, window.location.href)` inside a `try`/`catch` and logging compact `imagesLen`, `hosts`, and `lengths` arrays.

### Testing

author: cmilesio
body:
## Overview

This release finalizes the v2 API direction with a focus on **explicit behavior, predictable performance, and reduced surface area**.

The primary change is a move to **borrow-by-default semantics**, along with API cleanup, clarified mutability rules, and transparent benchmarking. Several legacy helpers and ambiguous behaviors were deprecated or removed to simplify usage and eliminate hidden costs.

## Breaking & Behavioral Changes

### Borrow-by-default construction

* `New` and `NewNumeric` no longer perform defensive copies.
* Collections now borrow the provided slice by default.
* This aligns behavior with standard Go slice semantics and removes hidden allocations.

```go
c := collection.New(items) // borrows items, no copy
```

### Explicit copying

* Copying is now opt-in.
* Use `Clone()` or `ItemsCopy()` to explicitly take ownership.

```go
owned := collection.New(items).Clone()
```

## API Simplifications & Deprecations

The following APIs were **removed or deprecated** to reduce redundancy, ambiguity, and overlapping semantics.

### Construction & ownership

* `Attach` Removed. Redundant after borrow-by-default `New`.

### Querying & filtering aliases

* `FindWhere` Removed. Use `FirstWhere`.
* `Where` Removed. Alias of `Filter`.
* Predicate-based `Contains` Removed. Replaced with value-based `Contains(collection, value)`.

### Transformation aliases

* `Pluck` Removed. Use `MapTo`.

### Mutation helpers (important)

* `Push` Removed. Use `Append`.
* `PushFront` Removed. Use `Prepend`.

These methods duplicated slice semantics and obscured whether an operation was mutating or allocating. Their removal makes mutation explicit and consistent across the API.

## Mutability & Method Classification

Methods are now consistently documented and classified as:

* **terminal** – end a chain and return a value
* **chainable** – return a collection for fluent pipelines
* **mutable** – modify the backing slice in place
* **immutable** – return a new collection

Notable clarifications:

* `Map` is explicitly mutable
* `Each` is readonly and chainable
* Many query helpers are terminal rather than fluent

This makes side effects explicit and easier to reason about.

## Benchmarks & Performance

### Dedicated benchmark documentation

* Added `BENCHMARKS.md` containing full raw benchmark data.
* Includes comparisons for:
  * `collection.New` (borrowed) vs `lo`
  * `collection.New().Clone()` (explicit copy) vs `lo`

### Condensed README benchmarks

* README now presents grouped, condensed tables:
  * Read-only operations
  * Transforming operations
  * Pipelines
  * Mutating operations
* Raw numbers remain available for auditability and transparency.

### Key observations

* Single operations are intentionally close to `lo`
* Chained pipelines often benefit significantly by avoiding intermediate allocations
* Copy costs are never normalized away or hidden

## Documentation Improvements

* Clear explanation of borrow-by-default behavior
* Explicit guidance on when to use `Clone()` and `ItemsCopy()`
* Improved examples and clarified semantics throughout
* Consistent terminology across the API and README

## Miscellaneous

* Increased test coverage
* Refined README layout and examples
* Minor wording and grammar corrections

## Summary

This release establishes a stable, predictable foundation going forward:

* Borrow by default
* Copy only when explicit
* Make mutation visible
* Measure real-world performance
* Reduce unnecessary API surface

It is intended as a long-term, coherent baseline for future evolution of the library.

Vercel deployment failing due to TypeScript type incompatibility: framer-motion v12 requires `ease` property to be typed as `Easing` (cubic bezier array), not a string literal.

## Changes

- Import `easeOut` from `@/lib/animations` 
- Replace string `"easeOut"` with typed constant in `cardVariants` transition
- Replace string `"easeOut"` with typed constant in principle bar animation

```typescript
// Before
transition: {
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: "easeOut",  // Type error: string not assignable to Easing
}

// After
import { easeOut } from "@/lib/animations";

transition: {
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: easeOut,  // Correctly typed as [0, 0, 0.58, 1]
}
```

The `easeOut` constant is already defined in `lib/animations.ts` as a properly typed cubic bezier array `[0, 0, 0.58, 1]`, consistent with existing patterns throughout the codebase.

body:
## Summary
- Implement PostgreSQL COPY TO BINARY protocol for faster source reads
- Add binary format parser (`pg_binary.rs`) with support for all common types
- Integrate with transfer engine via `use_copy_binary` flag (enabled by default for PG sources)
- Add benchmark tests comparing SELECT vs COPY performance

## Performance Results
Benchmark on StackOverflow Votes table (10.1M rows):

| Method | Throughput | Improvement |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| SELECT (1M rows) | 890K rows/s | baseline |
| COPY TO BINARY (1M rows) | 1.85M rows/s | **2.08x faster** |

End-to-end migration (PG→MSSQL upsert) showed ~5 second improvement for Votes table. The bottleneck is now on the MSSQL write side (MERGE operations), so the read optimization provides headroom for future write-side improvements.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for binary parser types (int, text, uuid, numeric, timestamp, etc.)
- [x] Benchmark tests: `cargo test --release -- bench_compare_copy_vs_select --ignored --nocapture`
- [x] Full migration test: 19.3M rows @ 83,557 rows/s

author: chenders
body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where the batch cause-of-death backfill script failed to parse Claude's responses when they were wrapped in markdown code fences (```json ... ```).

## Problem

Claude sometimes returns JSON responses wrapped in markdown code fences:
```
```json
{
  "cause": "cardiac arrest",
  "details": "...",
  "corrections": null
}
```
```

This caused `JSON.parse()` to fail with: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '`'`

## Solution

- Strip markdown code fences before parsing JSON
- Handle both ```json and plain ``` fences
- Ignore any text after the closing fence (e.g., notes about knowledge cutoff)

## Test plan

- [x] Added 3 new unit tests for code fence stripping
- [x] All 42 tests passing

### Motivation
- The profile editor modal's fixed width caused internal elements to be visually compressed and squeezed. 
- The modal should adapt to its content while remaining usable on small viewports. 
- The form layout needs to be more responsive so input fields don't collapse into cramped columns.

- Updated CSS in `src/components/ProfileEditorModal.vue` to set `.modal-card` to `width: fit-content`, `max-width: 92vw`, and `min-width: 320px` to let the dialog size to its content while capping viewport overflow.

author: satelllte
body:
## Description

During https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/32647, I noticed that if I push new commit(s), the runs from previous ones run until the end, which is redundant IMO. This change optimizes it.

Related GitHub docs:
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context

## Testing

For a test, I pushed "dummy commit" in this PR which cancelled the previous run.

## Additional notes

If this is something you'll consider to include into your workflow, the similar `concurrency` rules can be added to other workflows, but for now I started with the `ci.yml` workflow that takes the most of time to run (>10 minutes) and that is the best candidate to have this change to be applied on it.

So just me know if you want this to be applied to other workflows.

author: semeaipletinnya
body:
### Motivation
- Provide integration between silence-as-control and Poe Python bots by adding a dedicated adapter.
- Enable automatic silencing of bot responses based on coherence and drift signals.
- Expose a simple wrapper to maintain conversation history and apply the silence gate.

### Description
- Add `claude/adapters/poe_adapter.py` with constants `SILENCE`, `COHERENCE_THRESHOLD`, and `DRIFT_THRESHOLD`.
- Implement `should_silence` helper and `gated_bot_call` which calls `poe.call`, computes coherence and drift via provided callbacks, and returns `SILENCE` when thresholds are met.
- Provide `GatedPoeBot` class that stores `history`, exposes `call` to route through the gate and `reset` to clear history.

### Testing
- No automated tests or CI jobs were run as part of this change.

## Summary
Configure EAS Build for local Android APK generation with multi-environment support.

Closes #78

## Changes Made
- Configure eas.json with 3 build profiles (development, quality, production)
- Add EAS CLI ^16.28.0 and expo-dev-client ~6.0.14 to workspace

- Enable ProGuard, disable resource shrinking

- Move version/buildNumber constants to top of app.config.js
- Remove root eas.json (moved to apps/mobile)
- Update VS Code Java analysis settings for Android development
- Add APK/AAB patterns to root .gitignore

✅ Successfully built QA APK with `pnpm build:mobile:qa --local`
✅ APK installs and runs on device in QA environment

body:
## Problem
Multiple workflows running duplicate checks on both push and pull_request events:
- Branch Protection checks (ESLint, TypeScript, Prettier, Jest) ran twice
- CI workflow duplicated all branch-protection checks
- Issue State Sync ran on both push and PR events

This caused 18 total checks when only 12 unique checks were needed.

## Changes
- **Deleted** `ci.yml` - completely redundant with branch-protection.yml
- **Enhanced** branch-protection.yml - added codecov upload to preserve coverage reporting
- **Optimized** issue-state-sync.yml - only runs on pull_request events (not push)

## Result
Reduces GitHub Actions checks from **18 to 12** (removes 6 duplicates)

## Testing
This PR itself will demonstrate the fix - you should see:
- Only ONE set of Branch Protection checks (not duplicated for push/PR)
- NO "CI / lint-and-test" checks (workflow deleted)
- Only ONE Issue State Sync check

author: madmax983
body:
## Summary

Documents the critical requirement for WAL replay to maintain correct bi-temporal semantics after crash recovery.

## Context

PR #143 fixed time-travel queries returning deleted entities by closing the previous version's `transaction_time` before creating the tombstone. This fix works correctly for in-memory operations, but the same logic must be applied during WAL replay.

## Changes

Added detailed documentation in `PersistenceManager::recover()` explaining:

1. When replaying `DeleteNode`/`DeleteEdge` operations, the previous version's `transaction_time` MUST be closed
2. The tombstone's `temporal.transaction_time().start()` provides the correct `commit_timestamp`
3. Reference to `write_tx.rs::apply_changes()` for the implementation pattern

## Why This Matters

Without this fix during WAL replay:
- After a crash and recovery, deleted entities would reappear in time-travel queries
- The bug from issue #12 would manifest again after any crash

## Note

WAL replay is currently a stub (not fully implemented). This documentation ensures that when replay is implemented, the correct bi-temporal deletion semantics will be followed.

Related: Issue #12, PR #143

author: cody-no
body:
### Motivation

- Prevent users already in a call from being publicly informed they cannot join a locked voice channel while still enforcing access rules.
- Allow channel managers (via `manage_channels` permission) and configured voice-lock roles to bypass voice locks.
- Persist a configurable list of bypass roles so server operators can control who is exempt.

### Description

- Added `voice_lock_role_ids` to the `Config` dataclass and updated the `templates/config.json` template with an empty default list.
- Implemented helper functions `member_has_voice_lock_role`, `member_can_bypass_voice_lock`, and `is_voice_channel_locked` to centralise bypass and lock checks.
- Added an `on_voice_state_update` event handler that moves unauthorized joiners out of locked voice channels and only notifies the joining member by DM without messaging active callers.
- Updated `changelogs.txt` to document the voice-lock behaviour change.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for this change.
- Static code updates were limited to `modmail.py`, `templates/config.json`, and `changelogs.txt` and the project remains syntactically valid after edits.

💡 **What:** Optimized `MediaOptimizer::process` to use a single `preg_replace_callback` pass for both images and iframes instead of two sequential passes.

🎯 **Why:** Scanning large HTML strings multiple times (once for images, once for iframes) is inefficient O(N * 2). Combining them reduces this to O(N).

📊 **Impact:** Reduces CPU overhead during the media optimization phase, especially on content-heavy pages.

Please note: Since the PHP CLI is not available in this environment, this change was verified via rigorous manual code review and adherence to the project's existing logic patterns.

## Summary
Fixes the CI build failure and adds a verification step to prevent broken releases.

## Root Cause
Vite cannot handle query params in manifest paths (`index.html?context=popup`), causing production builds to fail while dev server worked fine.

- Created separate [popup.html](cci:7://file:///Users/fatihsolhan/Desktop/prompts-chat-extension/popup.html:0:0-0:0) and [sidepanel.html](cci:7://file:///Users/fatihsolhan/Desktop/prompts-chat-extension/sidepanel.html:0:0-0:0) entry points
- Each has `data-context` attribute on root div for context detection
- Updated manifest to reference the new HTML files

### CI Improvement
- Added "Verify build" step **before** semantic-release
- If build fails, CI fails early without creating a broken release

author: skroyc
body:
## Summary

Fixed the `ContextWarningMiddleware` to correctly track cumulative token usage across all conversation turns instead of using per-message token counts.

### Problem

The middleware was inspecting messages in reverse order and returning the first `total_tokens` value found, which was only the last message's token count. This caused warnings to trigger at incorrect thresholds:

- Turn 1: 1000 tokens → returned 1000 ✅
- Turn 2: 1500 tokens → returned 1500 ❌ (should be 2500)
- Turn 3: 3500 tokens (cumulative 6000) → returned 3500 ❌ (should be 6000)

At 6000/10000 tokens (60%), the old code would show 35% and not warn at the 50% threshold.

### Solution

1. Added `_cumulative_tokens = 0` instance variable in `__init__()`
2. Updated `after_model()` to accumulate token counts from each model response
3. Simplified `_get_current_token_count()` to return the cumulative total

### Testing

- All 30 tests in `tests/unit/test_langchain_middleware.py` pass
- Added 4 new tests specifically for cumulative token tracking
- Updated 5 existing tests to work with the new behavior

### Checklist

- [x] Cumulative token tracking implemented
- [x] Warnings trigger at correct 50%/75% thresholds
- [x] Tokens tracked correctly across 10+ turns
- [x] All tests pass

## Summary
- Refactored PBF parser to use single-pass implementation
- Reduced file I/O from 3 passes to 1 pass using DashMap for node coordinate caching
- Achieved 7.2% performance improvement on Shikoku dataset (7.17s → 6.65s)

## Changes
- `backend/src/importer/parser.rs`: Replaced 3-pass algorithm with single-pass using DashMap
- All node coordinates cached during way collection
- Pass 2 and Pass 3 eliminated and replaced with in-memory processing

## Performance Results
| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| File I/O | 3 passes | 1 pass | 66% reduction |
| Processing Time | 7.171s | 6.651s | 7.2% faster |
| Memory Usage | Medium | Medium-High | ~3.6MB increase |

**Benchmark conditions**: `shikoku-latest.osm.pbf`, bbox=132,33,135,35, 16,798 junctions

- [x] Code formatted (`cargo fmt --check`)

Establishes complete documentation infrastructure for kiku—an AI-powered child safety monitoring platform. Provides technical, business, and compliance documentation required for MVP launch, fundraising, and legal compliance.

## Structure (20 files, UTF-8, Russian)

### Technical Architecture
- **architecture/** — System design: backend/frontend/AI pipeline, data flows, cloud recommendations (AWS/GCP/Azure), Kubernetes, security (E2E encryption, KMS, RBAC, monitoring)
- **mvp/mvp_spec.md** — MVP scope: features, user flows, API contracts, TestFlight requirements
- **security/security_design.md** — Threat model, authentication (OAuth2/JWT), encryption stack, KMS, SIEM, incident response playbooks

### Business & Fundraising
- **investors/** — Pitch deck structure (12-15 slides), one-pager, TAM/SAM/SOM analysis ($15B market)
- **finance/** — 3-year financial model (3 scenarios), unit economics (LTV/CAC 6:1), CSV projections with quarterly breakdown

### Compliance & Legal
- **legal/** — Privacy policy draft (COPPA/GDPR), content moderation policy (5-level risk system), data room checklist
- **pilot/pilot_plan.md** — Pilot execution plan: 50-100 users, KPIs (NPS >50), security checklist, parental consent flows

### Infrastructure & Deployment
- **apple/testflight_instructions.md** — Complete iOS deployment: EAS configuration, App Store Connect setup, provisioning profiles, metadata requirements
- **infra/ci_cd.md** — GitHub Actions workflows, Kubernetes manifests, Terraform examples, secrets management (GitHub Secrets/Vault/AWS Secrets Manager)
- **.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md** — Security-focused PR checklist

### Product & Operations
- **team/team_roles.md** — Role definitions (CTO, Product, ML Engineer, SRE), compensation bands, equity allocation
- **roadmap/roadmap.md** — 24-month plan: PoC → MVP → TestFlight → Production → Global expansion
- **templates/** — Outreach templates (investors, schools, partners), data room structure

### Recommendations
- **license_recommendation.md** — MIT License analysis with dual-licensing strategy for enterprise features

## Security

All sensitive data uses placeholders:
```markdown
[FOUNDERS_EMAIL] — Email address
[APPLE_ID] — Apple Developer credentials  
[API_KEY] — Third-party API keys
```

Comprehensive secrets management documented in `docs/infra/ci_cd.md`:
- GitHub Secrets for CI/CD
- HashiCorp Vault for runtime
- AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager alternatives

## Compliance Disclaimers

Legal documents (`docs/legal/`) are **drafts** requiring professional legal review before production use. All include COPPA verifiable parental consent flows and GDPR data subject rights.

## Documentation Index

`docs/README.md` provides complete navigation, maintenance schedule, placeholder replacement guide, and confidentiality matrix by document type.

## Next Actions

1. Replace placeholders with production values
2. Legal counsel review of privacy/content policies
3. Apple Developer account setup
4. Replace `docs/architecture/diag.svg` with detailed architecture diagram
5. Configure GitHub Secrets for CI/CD workflows

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade @reduxjs/toolkit from 2.11.0 to 2.11.1.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
- The recommended version is **1 version** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **25 days ago**.
Release notes
Package name: @reduxjs/toolkit
  • 2.11.1 - 2025-12-08

    This bugfix release fixes an issue with our internal AbortSignal handling that was reported as causing an error in a rare reset situation. We've also restructured our publishing process to use NPM Trusted Publishing, and updated our TS support matrix to only support TS 5.4+.

    Changelog

    Publishing Changes

    We've previously done most of our releases semi-manually locally, with various release process CLI tools. With the changes to NPM publishing security and the recent wave of NPM attacks, we've updated our publishing process to solely use NPM Trusted Publishing via workflows. We've also done a hardening pass on our own CI setup.

    We had done a couple releases via CI workflows previously, and later semi-manual releases caused PNPM to warn that RTK was no longer trusted. This release should be trusted and will resolve that issue.

    Thanks to the e18e folks and their excellent guide at https://e18e.dev/docs/publishing for making this process easier!

    TS Support Matrix Updates

    We've previously mentioned rolling changes to our TS support matrix in release notes, but didn't officially document our support policy. We've added a description of the support policy (last 2 years of TS releases, matching DefinitelyTyped) and the current oldest TS version we support in the docs:

    • https://redux-toolkit.js.org/introduction/getting-started#typescript
    • https://redux-toolkit.js.org/usage/usage-with-typescript#introduction

    As of today, we've updated the support matrix to be TS 5.4+ . As always, it's possible RTK will work if you're using an earlier version of TS, but we don't test against earlier versions and don't support any issues with those versions.

    We have run an initial test with the upcoming TS 7.0 native tsgo release. We found a couple minor issues with our own TS build and test setup, but no obvious issues with using RTK with TS 7.0.

    Bug Fixes

    A user reported a rare edge case where the combination of resetApiState and retry() could lead to an error calling an AbortController. We've restructured our AbortController handling logic to avoid that (and simplified a bit of our internals in the process).

    What's Changed

    • Use trusted publishing and harden workflows by @ markerikson in #5152
    • Update TS typecheck matrix and add TS native job by @ markerikson in #5155
    • Officially document TS support by @ markerikson in #5158
    • Tweaks to AbortSignal logic by @ EskiMojo14 in #5150

    Full Changelog: v2.11.0...v2.11.1

  • 2.11.0 - 2025-11-23

    This feature release upgrades our Immer dependency to v11 to pick up the additional recent performance optimizations, adds a new refetchCachedPages option to allow only fetching the first cached page, and fixes an issue with regex ignore paths in the immutability middleware.

    Changelog

    Immer v11 Performance Improvements

    As described in the release notes for v2.10.0, we recently put significant effort into profiling Immer, and contributed several PRs that aimed to optimize its update performance.

    v2.10.0 updated to use Immer 10.2.0, which added the first smaller set of perf updates. That included a new Immer option to disable "strict iteration" to speed up iterating copied objects, and we specifically applied that change in RTK under the assumption that standard plain JS objects as Redux state shouldn't have unusual keys anyway. Overall, this appears to boost Immer update perf by ~+20% over v10.1 depending on update scenario.

author: alikhan126
body:
## CPPR-11: Build Temporal Dataset Splitter with Full BM25 Alignment

### Description

Creates a deterministic temporal dataset splitter for SEOSS-12 that partitions 112,408 issues into chronologically ordered train/val/test splits for continual learning evaluation.

**Key Feature**: Introduces a `proportional` missing timestamp assignment strategy that ensures 100% coverage—all issues are assigned to exactly one split, maintaining alignment with the BM25 matrix.

### Problem

The original splitter excluded 44,393 issues (39.5%) with missing timestamps, which broke alignment with the BM25 matrix of shape `(112408, vocab_size)`. This caused downstream training issues since the split indices didn't cover all matrix rows.

### Solution

Added a `proportional` strategy (now the default) that:
1. Assigns timestamped issues temporally (unchanged behavior)
2. For each project, computes train/val/test ratios from its timestamped issues
3. Randomly assigns missing-timestamp issues according to those project-specific ratios
4. Uses a seedable RNG for reproducibility

### Results on SEOSS-12

| Split | Before (exclude) | After (proportional) |
|-------|------------------|---------------------|
| Train | 47,852 (42.6%) | 79,001 (70.3%) |
| Val | 12,730 (11.3%) | 22,875 (20.3%) |
| Test | 7,433 (6.6%) | 10,532 (9.4%) |
| Excluded | 44,393 (39.5%) | **0 (0%)** |

### Changes

- **`src/cppr/data/splitter.py`**
  - Add `proportional` strategy with project-based ratio distribution
  - Add `MissingTimestampAssignment` dataclass for tracking
  - Add `random_seed` parameter for reproducible splits
  - Update `_build_summary()` to include assignment details

- **`src/cppr/data/__init__.py`**
  - Export `MissingTimestampAssignment`

- **`tests/unit/test_splitter.py`**
  - Add 12 new tests for proportional strategy
  - Test full coverage, reproducibility, and project ratio adherence

- **`data/splits/seoss12/`**
  - Updated split indices and summary with full coverage

### Invariants Maintained

- ✅ `len(train) + len(val) + len(test) == 112,408`
- ✅ No overlap between splits
- ✅ Temporal ordering preserved for timestamped issues
- ✅ Reproducible with `random_seed=42`
- ✅ All 12 projects in train, 10 in val/test (izpack/jbehave inactive post-2015)

### Usage

```python
from cppr.data import TemporalSplitter

# Default: proportional strategy with full coverage
splitter = TemporalSplitter(
    train_end="2015-12-31",
    val_end="2016-12-31",
    missing_strategy="proportional",  # default
    random_seed=42,
)
result = splitter.fit(df)

# All issues assigned
assert len(result.missing_timestamp_indices) == 0
total = len(result.train_indices) + len(result.val_indices) + len(result.test_indices)
assert total == len(df)
```

### Testing

- 37 splitter unit tests (12 new for proportional strategy)
- 234 total tests pass
- Linting clean (ruff, mypy)

### Blocks

CPPR-12 (Preprocessing Pipeline), CPPR-13 (Text Embeddings), CPPR-22 (Unified Training Loop)

author: shashikumar-ezhilarasu
body:
## Related Issue
This PR addresses the input validation concerns discussed in [PR #2197](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib/pull/2197) for FacemarkKazemi, where empty images could cause crashes during face detection or landmark fitting.

## Summary of Changes
- Added `CV_Assert(!image.empty())` in `FacemarkKazemiImpl::getFaces` and other critical functions to ensure empty images are caught early.
- Ensures that the library now safely handles cases where input images are missing or invalid.
- Minor code formatting and cleanup related to the assert additions.

This change improves stability and prevents runtime crashes without affecting existing functionality.

body:
### Motivation
- Remove the interactive/tool-backed toggle so the only write gate is the `WRITE_ALLOWED` boolean persisted/shared across workers.
- Avoid exposing an obsolete control in introspection and server config metadata.
- Simplify write-allow allowlists so no tool is implicitly exempt from the write gate.

### Description
- Deleted the `authorize_write_actions` tool from `main.py` and removed its persisted toggle behavior.
- Removed references to the toggle from introspection and server config by deleting the tool entry and the `toggle_tool` metadata.
- Cleared the allowlists (`_ALWAYS_WRITE_ENABLED_TOOLS` / `_ALWAYS_ALLOW_WRITE_TOOLS`) so no tool is implicitly allowed to bypass `WRITE_ALLOWED`.
- Removed the related persistence test and updated a small comment in `github_mcp/mcp_server/context.py` to reflect the general write gate wording.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change (no test run requested).
- Unit test `test_authorize_write_actions_persists_shared_gate` was removed/updated to reflect the deleted tool and toggle behavior.

author: velgail
body:
This pull request introduces a version management system to the project, modularizes and refactors the multimedia (media) functionality, and removes the use of precompiled headers for a simpler and more modern build configuration. The multimedia APIs and `Media` class are moved to a new dedicated module, and the project structure is updated accordingly. Additionally, a changelog is added to track notable changes.

**Versioning and Documentation:**

* Added a `CHANGELOG.md` file following Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning, with instructions and examples for future entries.
* Introduced a version management system: new `version.hpp`, `hsppp::get_version()`, and `hsppp::version()` functions, and build-time version info output in `WinMain.cpp`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f4db423bedadb8d5510c39170178c51df710ac3844983a4d82c55353334a7beR21-R57) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1de58f85e3782814458a95fe7e51617c5a213dd7651605117457c753bf2b812dR4-R25)

**Media/Multimedia Refactoring and Modularization:**

* Moved all multimedia-related APIs (`mmload`, `mmplay`, etc.) and the `Media` class from `hsppp_interrupt.ixx` to a new module `hsppp_media.ixx`, improving modularity and separation of concerns. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-88e20bdc8204a9a5383158cac021549a54fba3a039a7e14dbd172259b6f76834L277-L378) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3fed7242a9bb84aea739fe8b8e72bcd2f2889bd71f31e16a884f3c3be05c79deR1-R173) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9f4db423bedadb8d5510c39170178c51df710ac3844983a4d82c55353334a7beR21-R57)
* Updated project files (`HspppLib.vcxproj`, `.filters`) to include the new `hsppp_media.ixx` and adjust source/header listings accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8R159) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L171-R187) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-58aa9b352a736ebc094c6a558a9fdc9968eef235288a275e800da321b77b0931L30-L32) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-58aa9b352a736ebc094c6a558a9fdc9968eef235288a275e800da321b77b0931L42-R94)

**Build System and Structure Simplification:**

* Removed precompiled header files (`pch.h`, `pch.cpp`) and associated project configuration, streamlining the build process. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L101) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L119) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L141) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L152) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a1e9107c7b0c17308f0e637c6831c909a8ef85a589163ce495d1eb6bfe8428eaL1-L3) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0f4f9a5d6a035da6e270be53578a4033b042adc1aad4db7a40c7b68f9e136b2dL1-L5) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-3ef082345b1f01e3b8808ae9186a5668f7bcec311bcca96d4f886a5a4e071f8aL1-L13) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-58aa9b352a736ebc094c6a558a9fdc9968eef235288a275e800da321b77b0931L42-R94)
* Cleaned up unused or obsolete source and header references in the project and filters files, such as removing `Random.cpp` and reorganizing `.inl` includes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c2ca36cf452de09f9da5094614c40aca7df3f211021ee01a9ea1f9320eedc9e8L171-R187) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-58aa9b352a736ebc094c6a558a9fdc9968eef235288a275e800da321b77b0931L30-L32) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-58aa9b352a736ebc094c6a558a9fdc9968eef235288a275e800da321b77b0931L42-R94)

**Code Modernization:**

* Updated source files to use module imports (e.g., `import hsppp;`) instead of traditional includes for internal project code.

These changes collectively improve the maintainability, clarity, and modularity of the codebase, while also introducing proper version tracking and simplifying the build configuration.

author: arash-mp
body:
## Summary
This PR implements the Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) formulation to support moving mesh simulations in Neko. It introduces a new "ale_manager" to handle grid velocities and mesh deformation, modifies "fluid_pnpn" to include grid velocity terms, and updates the IO and checkpoints to support ALE simulations.

## Key Changes
### Core & Solver
* **New Module:** Added "src/ale/" containing "ale_manager.f90" (handles mesh motion logic) and core definitions.
* **Solver Update:** Modified "fluid_pnpn.f90" and "rhs_maker" to incorporate ALE advection terms (fluid velocity relative to mesh velocity).
* **BC type:** Implements a new "moving_boundary" boundary condition (**field_moving.f90**).

### IO & Checkpointing
* Updated "checkpoint.f90" and "chkp_file.f90" to save/restart simulations with moving meshes.

### Examples
* Added two new examples in "examples/":
    * "ocyl_cylinder3D": A cylinder hinged from the top and oscillate like a pendulum.
    * "ocyl_ellipse3D": A moving ellipse that simultaneously rotates around its axis.

## ToDo:
* GPU implementation (Currently CPU only).
* OIFS time-integration support.

## References:
Implementation is based on:
1- Fischer, P., Schmitt, M. and Tomboulides, A., 2017. Recent developments in spectral element simulations of moving-domain problems. Recent progress and modern challenges in applied mathematics, modeling and computational science, pp.213-244.
2- Ho, L.W., 1989. A Legendre spectral element method for simulation of incompressible unsteady viscous free-surface flows (Doctoral dissertation, Massachusetts Institute of Technology).

author: matte-ui
body:
### Motivation
- A lingering `guestMode` flag in `sessionStorage` can cause the client to continue treating a session as a guest after a successful login, preventing server-backed prefs and transaction metadata from loading.
- The code previously removed `localStorage` `guestMode` but left `sessionStorage` untouched, producing inconsistent guest detection across client modules.
- Clearing the in-session guest marker ensures the guest-aware guards and server-backed prefs/profile endpoints will be used for authenticated sessions.

### Description
- Remove `guestMode` from `sessionStorage` on successful login by adding `sessionStorage.removeItem('guestMode')` in `static/login.js` so both storages are cleared.
- The change is minimal and complements existing guest-aware helpers and the server-backed prefs/transactions endpoints so synced settings can load immediately after login.
- No other source files were modified in this patch.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: gurusai-voleti
body:
Automated: Migrate {target_path} from gsutil to gcloud storage

This CL is part of the on going effort to migrate from the legacy `gsutil` tool to the new and improved `gcloud storage` command-line interface.
`gcloud storage` is the recommended and modern tool for interacting with Google Cloud Storage, offering better performance, unified authentication, and a more consistent command structure with other `gcloud` components. 🚀

### Automation Details

This change was **generated automatically** by an agent that targets users of `gsutil`.
The transformations applied are based on the  [gsutil to gcloud storage migration guide](http://go/gsutil-gcloud-storage-migration-guide).

### ⚠️ Action Required: Please Review and Test Carefully

While we have based the automation on the migration guide, every use case is unique.
**It is crucial that you thoroughly test these changes in environments appropriate to your use-case before merging.**  
Be aware of potential differences between `gsutil` and `gcloud storage` that could impact your workflows.  
For instance, the structure of command output may have changed, requiring updates to any scripts that parse it. Similarly, command behavior can differ subtly; the `gcloud storage rsync` command has a different file deletion logic than `gsutil rsync`, which could lead to unintended file deletions.  

Our migration guides can help guide you through a list of mappings and some notable differences between the two tools.

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

Please verify that all your Cloud Storage operations continue to work as expected to avoid any potential disruptions in production.

### Support and Collaboration

The `GCS CLI` team is here to help! If you encounter any issues, have a complex use case that this automated change doesn't cover, or face any other blockers, please don't hesitate to reach out.
We are happy to work with you to test and adjust these changes as needed.

**Contact:** `gcs-cli-hyd@google.com`

We appreciate your partnership in this important migration effort!

## Summary
- Fix running mission tracking to use actual executing mission ID instead of current_mission
- Add real-time event streaming for OpenCode backend
- Fix missions staying Active after completion with OpenCode backend
- Improve iOS dashboard UI polish
- Add MCP server for desktop tools and Playwright integration

## Key Changes

### Mission Tracking Fix
Fixed a bug where clicking "New Mission" while another mission was running would:
- Show only the new mission in the Running Missions bar (missing the old running one)
- Display the Stop button incorrectly for the new empty mission

The fix adds `running_mission_id` to track the actual executing mission, separate from `current_mission` which can change when users create new missions.

### OpenCode Backend Improvements
- Real-time event streaming for better UI feedback
- Proper mission completion status handling

author: krissimon
body:
## Summary

Addresses critical documentation gaps identified in Book feature analysis:
- **Parallel for-each loops** were implemented (ef69c5f) but Chapter 32 stated they don't exist
- **Regex literals** (ARO-0037) deserve comprehensive coverage beyond Data Pipelines mention
- **SHA256 hash** algorithm should be explicitly documented

## Changes

### Chapter 32: Concurrency
- ✅ Remove "Parallel for loops" from exclusion list (line 177)
- ✅ Add comprehensive **Section 32.3: Parallel For-Each Loops**
  - Serial vs parallel iteration comparison
  - Execution model (DispatchQueue, thread pools)
  - Concurrency control (defaults to `System.coreCount`)
  - When to use parallel vs serial
  - Thread safety guarantees
  - Performance characteristics
  - Complete example from ParallelForEach

### Chapter 27: Control Flow
- ✅ Add comprehensive **Section 27.4: Regular Expression Matching**
  - Regex literal syntax `/pattern/flags`
  - Usage in match statements, filter actions, where clauses, split action
  - Common patterns library (email, URL, phone, dates, commands)
  - Best practices (anchors, escaping, readability)
  - Language comparison table (ARO vs JS/Ruby/Python/Java)

### Chapter 8: Computations
- ✅ Clarify hash operation uses **SHA256** algorithm
- ✅ Update SVG diagram to show hex output (`2c26b46b...`)
- ✅ Note cryptographic quality for security use cases

### Examples
- ✅ Fix outdated comments in `ParallelForEach/main.aro`
- ✅ Update to reflect true parallel execution in compiled code

### STRUCTURE.md
- ✅ Update Chapter 27 description to mention regex patterns

## Impact

**Before**: Users reading Chapter 32 would think parallel loops don't exist when they actually do (critical contradiction).

**After**: Complete documentation of parallel for-each with examples, best practices, and performance guidance.

**Before**: Regex only mentioned briefly in Data Pipelines chapter.

**After**: Comprehensive standalone section with 10+ common patterns, best practices, and cross-references.

## Files Changed
- `Book/TheLanguageGuide/Chapter32-Concurrency.md` (+150 lines)
- `Book/TheLanguageGuide/Chapter27-ControlFlow.md` (+300 lines)
- `Book/TheLanguageGuide/Chapter08-Computations.md` (minor clarifications)
- `Book/TheLanguageGuide/STRUCTURE.md` (updated description)
- `Examples/ParallelForEach/main.aro` (fixed stale comments)

- ✅ All cross-references validated
- ✅ SVG diagrams render correctly

author: crohns-kate
body:
The group booking name extraction was not running when gp was empty, only when it had placeholders. This caused names like "Jack Black" to be missed on the first turn, creating an infinite loop of asking.

Changes:
- Add `currentGpIsEmpty` and `needsMoreNames` checks to extraction condition
- Run extraction when: gp empty OR has placeholders OR has < 2 real names
- Add single name fallback when two names aren't extracted
- Accumulate names over multiple turns until 2 real names are captured
- Add detailed logging for debugging name extraction

This ensures names are captured immediately when spoken, before the AI responds, breaking the "ask twice" loop in group booking flows.

author: shinaoka
body:
## Summary

Move `unfold_split` from `tensor4all-linalg` to `tensor4all-tensor` as a generic tensor operation that can be used for various matrix decompositions beyond SVD.

## Changes

- **Moved `unfold_split` to `tensor4all-tensor`**: Now available as a general tensor operation
- **Made it generic**: Works with any element type (f64, Complex64, etc.) instead of having separate functions
- **Error handling**: Uses `anyhow::Result` instead of SVD-specific errors
- **Removed duplication**: Eliminated `unfold_split_c64` in favor of generic version
- **Updated SvdError**: Added `UnfoldError` wrapper, removed unused variants
- **Tests**: Updated to check for `UnfoldError`

## Benefits

- `unfold_split` is now available for other matrix decompositions (QR, LU, etc.)
- Cleaner separation of concerns: tensor operations in `tensor4all-tensor`, linear algebra in `tensor4all-linalg`
- More maintainable: single generic implementation instead of type-specific duplicates

## Testing

All existing tests pass (7/7).

body:
The requested feature "传入位置来控制连线的位置" (pass position to control connection line placement) was already fully implemented in PR #10. This PR adds verification and documentation.

## Connection Position Control

Three methods available in `add_connection`:

**Entry/Exit Points** (normalized 0-1 coordinates)
```python
add_connection(source, target,
    exit_x=1.0, exit_y=0.5,   # right-center
    entry_x=0.0, entry_y=0.5  # left-center
)
```

**Waypoints** (absolute pixels)
```python
add_connection(source, target,
    waypoints=[[250, 150], [250, 250]]
)
```

**Explicit Points** (absolute pixels)
```python
add_connection(source, target,
    source_point=[220, 130],
    target_point=[300, 230]
)
```

## Changes

- **verification script** (`verify_connection_positioning.py`) - validates all position control features
- **quick example** (`quick_example.py`) - demonstrates practical usage
- **documentation** (`FINAL_SUMMARY.md`, `ISSUE_RESOLUTION.md`) - comprehensive feature reference

All tests pass. Cross-platform compatible. Zero security alerts.

author: copilot
body:
Implements a production-ready development environment setup system with deterministic builds, offline support, security scanning, and agent-ready architecture.

## Core Infrastructure

- **Idempotent installation**: Version checks before install, skip already-installed tools, status tracking (INSTALLED/SKIPPED/FAILED)
- **Version locking**: All tools pinned in `config/versions.env`, asdf-compatible `.tool-versions`, optional `SETUP_ALLOW_LATEST` override
- **Offline/air-gap support**: `artifacts/` directory for local installers with auto-detection
- **JSON reports**: `setup-report.json` with metadata + backup mechanism, `.mcp/context.json` for agent context
- **Shell-agnostic environment**: `env.d/` structure sourced by Bash/Zsh/Fish/PowerShell

## Security

- **Pre-commit hooks**: ruff (Python), eslint (JS/TS), cargo fmt/clippy (Rust)
- **Secret scanning**: Gitleaks configuration with allowlists
- **Dependency auditing**: npm/pip vulnerability checks via GitHub Actions
- **Secure downloads**: Download-then-execute pattern (no pipe-to-bash)

```bash
# Before: Security risk
curl https://example.com/install.sh | bash

# After: Safer approach
curl https://example.com/install.sh -o /tmp/install.sh
bash /tmp/install.sh
rm /tmp/install.sh
```

## Multi-Agent Architecture

- **5 specialized agents**: orchestrator, backend (Python/Rust), frontend (TS/React), devops (CI/CD), testing (QA)
- **3 reusable skills**: code-analysis, testing, documentation
- **MCP context generation**: Auto-generated environment metadata for agent consumption

## Cross-Platform Support

- **Bash scripts** (Linux/macOS): `setup.sh`, `validate.sh`, `smoke-test.sh`
- **PowerShell scripts** (Windows): `setup.ps1`, `validate.ps1`, `smoke-test.ps1`
- **DevContainer**: Auto-setup via `post-create.sh`, GitHub Codespaces ready

## Managed Tools

| Tool | Version | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| nvm | 0.39.7 | Node version management |
| Node.js | 20.11.0 | JavaScript runtime |
| pnpm | 8.15.1 | Package manager |
| Miniconda | latest | Python environment |
| uv/uvx | 0.1.18 | Fast Python tooling |
| Rust | 1.75.0 | Systems programming |

## GitHub Workflows

- **Security scan**: Weekly gitleaks + dependency audits (npm/pip)
- **Codespace setup**: Multi-platform validation (Linux/macOS/Windows)

## Documentation

- **INSTALLATION.md**: Complete setup guide with offline instructions
- **SECURITY.md**: Security features, vulnerability reporting, best practices
- **TROUBLESHOOTING.md**: Common issues with solutions
- **copilot-instructions.md**: Development guidelines for AI assistance

## Usage

```bash
# Interactive setup
bash quickstart.sh

# Direct installation
bash scripts/validate.sh    # Pre-flight checks
bash scripts/setup.sh        # Run installation
bash scripts/smoke-test.sh   # Verify installation

# Windows
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

**Files**: 40 configuration/script files across 12 directories  
**Lines**: ~15,000 LOC  
**Coverage**: All 12 requirements from problem statement

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# 🚀 Enterprise-Grade Development Environment Setup

Erstelle ein **production-ready** Setup-Repository mit allen Enterprise-Features eingebaut.

## 🎯 Kern-Features (NICHT optional - ALLES rein!)

### 1. **Idempotenz-Level Maximum**
Setup muss **mehrfach** laufen können ohne Seiteneffekte.
- Vor jeder Installation: Version Check + Skip mit grünem Status
- Summary am Ende: `INSTALLED / SKIPPED / FAILED`
- Keine redundanten Downloads
- CI-optimiert

### 2. **Deterministische Version Locks**
Keine Überraschungen in CI/CD.
- `versions.env` mit gepinnten Versionen
- Node, pnpm, Python, Rust **explizit** pinnen
- Optional: `SETUP_ALLOW_LATEST=true` Flag für Dev
- Default: **strikte Versionen**

### 3. **Offline-Fallback (Enterprise-Ready)**
Corporate-Netzwerke blocken Installer.
- `artifacts/` Ordner für lokale Binaries
- Wenn vorhanden: **lokale Installation bevorzugen**
- Sonst: normaler Download
- Air-gap ready

### 4. **Post-Setup Health Report (JSON)**
Maschinell lesbar für Automatisierung.
- `setup-report.json` generieren
- Tool, Version, Path, Status
- MCP-Agent ready
- Telemetrie-kompatibel

### 5. **Shell-Agnostic ENV Handling**
Kein Profil-Spaghetti mehr.
- Zentrale `env.d/` Struktur
- Shells sourcen nur generierte Files
- Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell Support

### 6. **Security-Baseline (Integriert)**
Security by default, nicht optional.
- **pre-commit** hooks:
  - `ruff` (Python)
  - `eslint` (TypeScript)
  - `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy` (Rust)
- **gitleaks** für Secret Scanning
- `.env` Leak Prevention
- Default: deny commits with secrets

### 7. **MCP/Agent-Ready Context**
OpenCode + Agents = MCP Context.
- `.mcp/context.json` generieren:
  - OS, Arch, Toolchain
  - Repo-Rollen
  - Installed Tools
- Agents können sofort loslegen

### 8. **One-Shot Smoke Test**
Nach Installation: automatischer Test.
- Node: `node --version`

- pnpm: `pnpm store path`

## Tiered Rate Limiting Implementation - Complete ✅

### Summary
Successfully implemented comprehensive tiered rate limiting with role-based access control, operation-specific limits, and configurable exemptions. All requirements from the issue have been addressed.

### Completed Tasks
- [x] Analyze current rate limiting implementation
- [x] Add rate limiting environment variables to config
- [x] Create tiered rate limiting functions for different user roles
- [x] Add dynamic rate limit helpers for read vs write operations
- [x] Update rate_limit.py with role-based and operation-based limits
- [x] Add rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-*) to responses
- [x] Implement exemption logic for superadmin users
- [x] Add IP-based exemption support
- [x] Update .env.example with new rate limiting configuration
- [x] Create comprehensive tests for tiered rate limiting
- [x] Update documentation with new rate limiting features
- [x] Address code review feedback
- [x] Run security scan with CodeQL
- [x] Fix all lint and format issues

### Features Implemented

#### 1. Tiered Rate Limiting by Role
- **Unauthenticated**: 20/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_UNAUTHENTICATED`)
- **ATTENDANT**: 100/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_ATTENDANT`)
- **MANAGER**: 200/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_MANAGER`)
- **ADMIN**: 500/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN`)
- **OWNER**: 1000/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_OWNER`)
- **Superadmin**: Unlimited (automatically exempt)

#### 2. Operation-Based Limits
- Read operations (GET): 2x base limit (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_READ_MULTIPLIER`)
- Write operations (POST/PUT/DELETE): 1x base limit (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_WRITE_MULTIPLIER`)

#### 3. Exemption Support
- **Superadmin users**: Automatically exempt from all rate limits
- **IP-based exemptions**: Configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_EXEMPT_IPS` (comma-separated list)

#### 4. Rate Limit Headers
All responses include:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum requests allowed
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining (429 responses)
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Seconds until limit resets
- `Retry-After`: Standard retry header

#### 5. Full Configuration via Environment Variables
All rate limits are configurable without code changes, making it easy to adjust per environment.

### Files Changed
- `app/core/config.py`: Added rate limiting configuration
- `app/core/rate_limit.py`: Implemented tiered rate limiting logic

author: copilot
body:
When the last player revealed their card for the first time, they saw their role (e.g., "Civil", "Intruso") instead of their word. This occurred because `allRevealed` was set to `true` in the same render cycle as the reveal, causing React's state batching to apply both updates simultaneously.

## Changes

- Track which players have hidden their card at least once via `hasHiddenCard` state
- Pass `hasSeenCard` prop to `PlayerCard` based on `hasHiddenCard` membership
- Use `!hasSeenCard` instead of `!allRevealed` to determine Phase 1 (word) vs Phase 2 (role)

```tsx
// Before: allRevealed triggered phase change prematurely
{!allRevealed ? <ShowWord /> : <ShowRole />}

// After: phase determined by individual player history
{!hasSeenCard ? <ShowWord /> : <ShowRole />}
```

## Result

All players, including the last one, now see their word on first reveal:

**First reveal (Phase 1):**
![Bob sees his word "Árvore" on first reveal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6892bf5-0c6d-40c6-9504-ed06f99c2758)

**Subsequent reveal (Phase 2):**
![Bob sees his role "Intruso" after hiding once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70d4a981-263a-4cc1-9464-346ed8166938)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> In the Intruso game, when the last player reveals their card for the first time, they only see their role (e.g., "Civil", "Intruso", "Mr. White") instead of seeing their word first like all other players.
> 
> ## Root Cause
> 
> In `src/components/intruso/IntrusoGame.tsx`, the `toggleCard` function sets `allRevealed` to `true` inside the `setRevealedOnce` callback when the last player reveals their card:
> 
> ```tsx
> if (newSet.size === players.length) {
>   setAllRevealed(true);
> }
> ```
> 
> The problem is that this state update is batched with the reveal action, so when the `PlayerCard` component renders, `allRevealed` is already `true`, causing it to show Phase 2 (the role) instead of Phase 1 (the word).
> 
> ## Expected Behavior
> 
> When any player (including the last player) reveals their card for the **first time**, they should see:
> 1. Their word (for civilians and undercover) or the "no word" message (for Mr. White)
> 2. Only on subsequent reveals (after all players have seen their cards once) should the role be shown
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Track whether the current player has already seen their card during this reveal. The `PlayerCard` component should check if this is the player's first time viewing the card, and if so, show the word regardless of the `allRevealed` state.
> 
> One approach is to pass an additional prop indicating whether this specific player has seen their card before (`hasSeenCard`), and use that to determine what to show:
> - If `!hasSeenCard` (first reveal): show the word (Phase 1)
> - If `hasSeenCard` (subsequent reveals): show the role (Phase 2)
> 
> This way, even when the last player reveals their card and triggers `allRevealed`, they will still see their word on that first reveal because `hasSeenCard` for them would still be `false` at that moment.


</details>

body:
### Motivation
- Modernize type hints to Python 3.10+ builtin generics for consistency across modules such as the DSPy pipeline and tracer adapters.
- Defer heavy import costs by making participatory-agency training symbols lazy to avoid eager module loading.
- Make attribution extraction and tracer adapters more robust for tiny / test models and empty responses.
- Provide an optional, well-integrated participatory-agency multi-head value decomposition package and safe integration helpers.

### Description
- Replaced `typing` generics with builtins (e.g. `Dict`/`List` → `dict`/`list`) in `src/mindful_trace_gepa/dspy_modules/pipeline.py` and other files and updated related annotations like `dict[str, Any] | None` and `list[ModuleResult]`.
- Added a new `gepa_mindfulness/participatory_agency` package (configs, `values`, `heads`, `training`, `interpretability`, `governance`) and integration helpers in `gepa_mindfulness/integrations/participatory_agency_integration.py` that register the built head via `model.add_module("participatory_value_head", head)` when supported and fall back to `setattr` otherwise.
- Hardened attribution logic in `gepa_mindfulness/interpret/attribution_graphs.py` by introducing `use_fast_gradients` (fast-unit-gradients fallback for tiny models), guarding empty response token tensors during gradient computation, switching threshold semantics to `score < threshold` so nodes equal to the threshold are included, and ensuring a top candidate is selected when no nodes exceed the threshold.
- Improved `CircuitTracerAdapter` and `TraceResult` (`gepa_mindfulness/core/circuit_tracer_adapter.py`) by adding a `TraceProtocol` typing abstraction, including the raw `trace` payload in results, and updating types to builtin generics; also reordered standard-library imports in `gepa_mindfulness/training/grpo_trainer.py` per style.

body:
Implements a complete workflow specification generator that transforms natural language goals into structured, validated workflow specs via LLM orchestration.

## Core Components

### Validation Layer (`packages/kernel/`)
- **Zod schemas** for type-safe validation of workflow specs, tasks, permissions, retry configs, sandbox settings
- Helper function `convertJSONToWorkflowSpec()` handles JSON (Record) → runtime type (Map) conversion
- New event types: `LLM_PROMPT_GENERATED`, `LLM_RESPONSE_RECEIVED`

### LLM Orchestration (`apps/console/src/workflow-generator.ts`)
- Generates 3-6 tasks from natural language with risk tier assignment
- Creates sequential dependency chains automatically
- Adds retry configs for HIGH/CRITICAL risk tasks
- Mock implementation ready for real LLM API swap
- Complete audit logging via EventLog

### API Layer (`apps/console/src/api-server.ts`)
- `POST /api/workflows/generate` - accepts goal text, returns structured spec
- `POST /api/workflows/validate` - validates against Zod schema
- `GET /wizard` - serves UI (needs rate limiting for production)

### UI (`apps/console/src/ui/workflow-wizard.html`)
Three-step wizard: goal input → spec preview with editing → validation results

## Example Usage

```typescript
const generator = new WorkflowGenerator(eventLog);

const result = await generator.generateWorkflow({
  goal: 'Reconcile bank transactions with internal ledger',
  constraints: ['Complete within 5 minutes'],
  preferredTools: ['database', 'email'],
  riskTolerance: 'HIGH'
});

// Returns WorkflowSpec with 3-6 tasks, sequential dependencies,
// retry configs, and safety policy
```

## Security

- Authentication + permission checks on all endpoints
- All LLM interactions logged to audit trail
- Zod validation prevents malformed inputs
- **Note**: `/wizard` route lacks rate limiting (see `SECURITY_SUMMARY.md`)

## Documentation

- `WORKFLOW_GENERATOR_README.md` - API reference and usage
- `WORKFLOW_GENERATOR_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - architecture details
- `SECURITY_SUMMARY.md` - threat model and recommendations
- `example-workflow-generator.ts` - programmatic usage examples

## Testing

35+ test cases covering schema validation and generator logic. Tests are structured but blocked by pre-existing repository dependency issues (unrelated to this PR).

body:
SDK source distribution enables trivial bypass development through complete detection logic analysis. Binary-only distribution raises the reverse engineering barrier while preserving integration capability.

## Changes

**Packaging automation**
- `scripts/package_sdk.sh` - Linux/macOS packaging with platform-specific tooling (readelf/otool, GNU/BSD strip)
- `scripts/package_sdk.ps1` - Windows packaging with PowerShell
- Automated: build Release → strip symbols → filter headers → archive → checksum

**Distribution structure**
```
SentinelSDK-1.0.0-{platform}-{arch}/
├── lib/              # Stripped binaries (.so/.dylib/.dll)
├── include/          # SentinelSDK.hpp + minimal Core types only
├── docs/             # Integration guide, license verification
└── examples/         # Functional integration demo
```

**Security guarantees**
- Zero `.cpp` files (except example)
- Zero internal headers (`src/SDK/src/Internal/*` excluded)
- Symbols stripped: `strip --strip-debug` (Linux), `strip -S` (macOS), no `.pdb` (Windows)
- Library symlinks for SONAME/install_name resolution

**License enforcement**
- JWT tokens with ES256 signatures
- Game-specific binding via `game_id`
- Online/offline validation modes

## Integration

Studios integrate using only distributed artifacts:

```cpp
#include <SentinelSDK.hpp>

Sentinel::SDK::Configuration config = Sentinel::SDK::Configuration::Default();
config.license_key = "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIs...";
config.game_id = "studio-game-id";
Sentinel::SDK::Initialize(&config);
```

No source access required. Detection logic remains opaque.

## Verification

Package tested with clean-room integration:
- Example builds with distributed files only
- `file lib/libSentinelSDK.so` confirms "stripped"
- `find . -name "*.cpp" | grep -v examples` returns empty
- SDK initializes and functions correctly

Package size: 408KB compressed

author: rtfeldman
body:
This fixes the remaining case in issue #8851 where the formatter was not idempotent for expressions like `0->b .c()`.

The problem: when a field_access follows a local_dispatch where the right side is a plain identifier (not an apply), the formatter was outputting `0->b.c()` which the parser interprets as calling a qualified function `b.c` instead of field access on `0->b`. On the next formatting pass, the `()` would be stripped, producing `0->b.c`.

The fix extends the existing handling (for zero-arg applies) to also cover plain identifiers. Now expressions like `0->b .c()` correctly format to `0->b().c()` which is stable on subsequent formatting passes.

- Extended the field_access formatting logic to handle both plain identifiers and zero-arg applies
- Added test snapshot for the new case (`0->b .c()`)
- Updated existing snapshot that was affected by the fix

Fixes #8851

## Summary

Implements the complete database schema for Haushaltsbuch (personal finance app):

- **9 PostgreSQL migrations** with RLS policies for single-household access
- **Seed data** with German categories and vendor rules for common merchants
- **TypeScript type definitions** for full type safety with Supabase client

## Database Schema

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `accounts` | Bank accounts (checking, credit_card) |
| `categories` | Hierarchical spending categories |
| `transactions` | Core transaction records |
| `vendor_rules` | Pattern matching for auto-categorization |
| `import_jobs` | PDF import tracking |
| `comments` | Transaction annotations |
| `category_overrides` | Audit trail for category changes |

### Views
- `monthly_summary` - Aggregates by month/category
- `category_summary` - All-time category totals
- `needs_review` - Transactions requiring attention

## Key Design Decisions

- **Amounts stored as INTEGER (cents)** with separate `direction` enum (debit/credit)
- **Hierarchical categories** using adjacency list (parent_id)
- **JSONB** for flexible error/warning storage in import_jobs
- **RLS** enabled on all tables with `authenticated = access` pattern

## Seed Data

- 2 default accounts: ING Girokonto, DKB Kreditkarte
- 25 German categories in 2-level hierarchy (Wohnen, Lebensmittel, Transport, etc.)
- 35 vendor rules for common German merchants (EDEKA, REWE, Deutsche Bahn, etc.)

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `supabase db push --linked` to apply migrations to Supabase Cloud
- [ ] Verify tables created in Supabase dashboard
- [ ] Run `supabase db reset` locally (requires Docker) to test with seed data
- [ ] Confirm TypeScript types compile without errors: `cd web && npm run build`

supabase db push --linked
